problem:
Find ${e}^{At}$ for $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -5 & -2\end{aligned}].$ 

*Hint: The eigenvalues of $A$ are $\pm \text{i}.$*

| ${e}^{At}=\,\,$ |  | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)$ | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)$ |  |  |

feedback.problem:
Find ${e}^{At}$ for $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -13 & -1\end{aligned}].$ 

*Hint: The eigenvalues of $A$ are $\pm 5\text{i}.$*

| ${e}^{At}=\frac{1}{5}\,\,$ |  | $5\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)$ | $2\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)$ |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
We have a square matrix of dimension $n=2.$ Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{At} & ={\alpha }_{1}At+{\alpha }_{0}I \\  & ={\alpha }_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -13 & -1\end{aligned}]t+{\alpha }_{0}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & 2{\alpha }_{1}t \\ -13{\alpha }_{1}t & -{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ are functions to be determined.

Consider the polynomial $r(\lambda )={\alpha }_{1}\lambda +{\alpha }_{0}.$ The eigenvalues or $At$ are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=5\text{i}t,\,{\lambda }_{2}=-5\text{i}t,
$$

which are complex conjugates. Thus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(5\text{i}t) & ={e}^{5\text{i}t} \\ {\alpha }_{1}\cdot 5\text{i}t+{\alpha }_{0} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ {\alpha }_{0}+5{\alpha }_{1}\text{i}t & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we equate the real and imaginary parts, and solve for ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{0}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\ 5{\alpha }_{1}t=\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{1}=\frac{1}{5t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ {\alpha }_{0}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ into the expressions for the required entries of ${e}^{At},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}-13{\alpha }_{1}t & =-13\cdot \frac{1}{5t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\cdot t \\  & =-\frac{13}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ -{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & =-\frac{1}{5t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\cdot t+\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t))\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{e}^{At}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) & 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ -13\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) & 5\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}].
$$
